summary: A research report was developed on two Earth locations proposed as analogs to Mars. To achieve this, the team conducted an in-depth analysis of the Red Planet's primary characteristics and evaluated different regions on Earth in order to establish comparative baselines within a viable scope of study. In this way, sites matching Martian conditions were identified to contribute to NASA's future research and testing, allowing space scenarios to be simulated and validated safely and accessibly prior to launching missions into space.
details:
The project presented consists of a research report focused on identifying two locations on Earth that exhibit characteristics analogous to those found on Mars. Our objective is to contribute to research and the development of testing activities related to the exploration of the Red Planet by taking advantage of environments found here on Earth.

During our research, we identified the Gobi Desert, located between northern China and southern Mongolia, as a region of interest due to its geological and environmental characteristics, some of which present similarities to conditions on Mars. This report describes the main features we identified as relevant for establishing this analogy. We also considered the Deccan Traps, located in west-central India, because this geological formation is composed primarily of basalt, which is also one of the predominant materials on the Martian surface. In addition, it exhibits mineralogical and geological characteristics of interest for planetary research.

To carry out this project, we conducted an extensive search and collection of information using data and resources provided by NASA, open-access sources cited in this report, artificial intelligence tools such as Claude and Gemini, Google's search engine, and interactive solar system simulators that allow users to explore and visualize information about celestial bodies.

In our analysis of both locations, we considered several factors to establish comparisons with Mars, including mineralogy, radiation, geology, topographical features, terrain composition and conditions, temperature, lighting, environmental extremes, the presence of water, ice, permafrost, wind, erosion, and biosignatures. These elements allowed us to identify the main similarities and differences between the two locations and assess their potential as analog environments for future research and space exploration missions.
